Messages.Author: Rafid Armani
Messages.Body:
Just to test myself before tomorrow <evil grin>

1-Vampire A is in combat with vampire B. Vampire A use agg damage as
a strike. Who can play Rotshreck and who goes to torpor for that ?

2-A vampire is equiped with a bastard sword, he plays a Torn Signpost
in superior, he strikes for how much ? What if he has +1 hand damage
written in his description ?

3-It is said in the clarifications that a vampire's capacity can never
be reduced below one. Why is it said also that a vampire's capacity
can never be less than zero ? What could you do anyway with a zero
capacity vampire ?

4- a) When a player is ousted, which cards leave the table with him ?
All the ones that he controls (Charnas the Imp, Fame, etc.)?

b) What about Millicent Smith if he's the one who brought it on the
table but is not the controller when he is ousted ?

c) If I control a vampire of the ousted Methuselah (Grave Robbing), do
all the masters (and retainers) that methuselah had put on that
vampire leave play ?

5-Can a methuselah choose to burn a vampire BEFORE the loss of one
pool for Antediluvian Awakening (the card says pay one pool at the
START of untap phase) ?

6-If I play a Burning Wrath, and then I play a Primal Insctincts and
choose a new strike, do my vampire have to pay the cost of BW ?

7-If I play Flesh of Marble in superior and the opposing vampire
strikes me for 1 normal + 1 aggravated, do I have the choice of which
damage I take ?

8-Vampire A (10 blood points on him) stikes with a sup Burning Wrath
(3 agg), Vampire B (10 blood points on him) strikes with sup Theft of
Vitae (steal 2) ; how does it finish (how much blood on each vampire)
?

9-Parity Shift : do I have to reallocate the pool among ALL other
methuselahs, or do I have the choice to keep it for me or give it all
to one of the methuselah ?

10-Methuselah A has Koko with the Rack on him. Methuselah B steals
Koko with a Grave Robbing (or a Hostile Takeover). What happens with
the Rack ?

11-Is the Spawning Pool usable at long range ?

Thank you very much for your time,

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Rafid Armani wrote:
> 1-Vampire A is in combat with vampire B. Vampire A use agg damage as
> a strike. Who can play Rotshreck and who goes to torpor for that ?

Any Methuselah can play Rotschreck except for the Methuselah whose turn
it is.
Rotschreck is played on the vampire against whom the minion is attempting
to use aggravated damage. In the example, vampire B goes to torpor.

> 2-A vampire is equiped with a bastard sword, he plays a Torn Signpost
> in superior, he strikes for how much ? What if he has +1 hand damage
> written in his description ?

Assuming he strikes with the Bastard Sword, he strikes for 4 damage
(Torn Signpost sets his strength to 3, and the sword inflicted strength+1
damage).
If the vampire has +1 strength (due to his special ability, for example),
he'll inflict 5 damage (one additional for the strength bonus).

> 3-It is said in the clarifications that a vampire's capacity can never
> be reduced below one. Why is it said also that a vampire's capacity
> can never be less than zero ? What could you do anyway with a zero
> capacity vampire ?

A vampire's capacity can never go below 1. This is a change from a previous
ruling.

> 4- a) When a player is ousted, which cards leave the table with him ?
> All the ones that he controls (Charnas the Imp, Fame, etc.)?

The ones that she controls.

> b) What about Millicent Smith if he's the one who brought it on the
> table but is not the controller when he is ousted ?

If he doesn't control it, the it is not burned.

> c) If I control a vampire of the ousted Methuselah (Grave Robbing), do
> all the masters (and retainers) that methuselah had put on that
> vampire leave play ?

Only the ones that the ousted Methuselah controls.
This is typically just the Master cards. Expicit card text (or errata)
is needed to maintain control of non-master library cards ("minion cards")

> 5-Can a methuselah choose to burn a vampire BEFORE the loss of one
> pool for Antediluvian Awakening (the card says pay one pool at the
> START of untap phase) ?

Yes. The only effect that happens at the START of the untap phase
is the untapping of all of one's cards. All other effects can be
ordered as one wishes.

> 6-If I play a Burning Wrath, and then I play a Primal Insctincts and
> choose a new strike, do my vampire have to pay the cost of BW ?

Yes, since Primal Instrincts says nothing about regaining the blood
you've already spent playing the cancelled strike.

> 7-If I play Flesh of Marble in superior and the opposing vampire
> strikes me for 1 normal + 1 aggravated, do I have the choice of which
> damage I take ?

You choose, yes.

> 8-Vampire A (10 blood points on him) stikes with a sup Burning Wrath
> (3 agg), Vampire B (10 blood points on him) strikes with sup Theft of
> Vitae (steal 2) ; how does it finish (how much blood on each vampire)
> ?

Depends on the capacity of vampire B.
Stolen blood in excess of his capacity drains off immediately (as always),
which is before it can be used to heal damage or prevent destruction.

vamp A ends with 5 blood (burned 3 for Wrath, lost 2 for theft).
vamp A ends in torpor with MAX(cap,12)-2 blood (12 or his capacity for
the theft, followed by a loss of two blood to prevent destruction).

> 9-Parity Shift : do I have to reallocate the pool among ALL other
> methuselahs, or do I have the choice to keep it for me or give it all
> to one of the methuselah ?

You can exclude some Methuselahs, as you see fit.

> 10-Methuselah A has Koko with the Rack on him. Methuselah B steals
> Koko with a Grave Robbing (or a Hostile Takeover). What happens with
> the Rack ?

Nothing. It continues to be able to "feed" Koko, and is still controlled
by Meth A.

> 11-Is the Spawning Pool usable at long range ?

Yes.

Yes.

>Now I'm totally lost...I always thought that what made the difference
>between Fists of Death and Torn Signpost, was that the latter nullified
>any modifying damage that was on the vampire before the TS was played.

Not really. The +1 hand damage from the vampire is permanent. It's not
a "played" or "unplayed" thing.

The major difference between Fists of Death and Torn Signpost is that
Fists of Death is stackable, but Torn Signpost isn't - so FoD has the
blood cost.

>If the vampire had +1 hand damage he'd not benefit from it with TS was
>played, because TS sets the strength to 3 and doesn't increase the
>strength with 2 as Fists of Death does. So how is FS better than TS
>with your ruling above? It even costs one blood.

Fists of Death isn't intended to be "better" or "worse".

One slight change from Jyhad to V:TES was that the vampires who
previously said 2 hand damage (e.g. Bianca) now say +1 hand damage. So,
in Jyhad, Torn Signpost was a little different, but not vastly.

However, Fists of Death is still playable, if you want to. You can play
several in one round, *and* get some bonus for it, if you find you've
suddenly picked up three at once. You can stack it on top of Torn
Signpost, too.

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Sat, 26 Aug 2000 14:53:40 GMT, can...@my-deja.com wrote:

>Now I'm totally lost...I always thought that what made the difference
>between Fists of Death and Torn Signpost, was that the latter nullified
>any modifying damage that was on the vampire before the TS was played.

>If the vampire had +1 hand damage he'd not benefit from it with TS was
>played, because TS sets the strength to 3 and doesn't increase the
>strength with 2 as Fists of Death does. So how is FS better than TS
>with your ruling above? It even costs one blood.

(all examples assume superior Potence)

Torn Signpost sets your base strength to 3. If you have pre-existing
modifiers such as +1 base strength, these apply now. But no matter
how many Torn Signposts you play, you never get more than 3 to start
with. And it's free.

Fists of Death gives you an additional +2 strength, pure and simple.
You can play Torn Signpost first, and then Fists of Death, and get +4
strength. If you play in the other order, though, you get only +2
strength, since Torn Signpost merely SETS your strength instead of
modifying it. And Fists of Death doesn't modify base strength, so it
wouldn't apply afterwards in the same way. For the stackability, it
costs a blood.

Increased Strength generally works almost exactly like Fists of Death,
except for its free cost it only applies a damage modifier to Potence
strike cards - so you cannot Increased Strength/Blur, you must use FoD
or Torn Signpost. You can, however, IS/Undead Strength, and the
results look just the same as if you had used a Signpost or Fists.

Is Fists of Death better than Torn Signpost? -shrug- I tend to
include a few Fists (2-3) in most decks, just for that stackability in
case I need to knock over a full 10-cap - play TS/FoD, strike for 5,
Blur at inferior for another, and now he's empty. Taste, press with
the Grapple and bop him once more. Or, if you're just using Potence,
TS/FoD/Undead Strength for 7, Taste, press with the Grapple, and smack
for 5 next round (eliminates even IC members!). You may have to
Grapple him twice, but big guys take more effort. You can't do this
as easily with just Torn Signpost - need to use multiple strike cards
or have superior CEL.
